questions.q: Explain in your own words why Ambedkar includes Jyotiba Phule (xka/h th) as a reference in this essay. What specific purpose does Phule serve in Ambedkar's argument about caste?
questions.a: Ambedkar cites Phule to establish an ideological lineage — Phule's "tkfrHksn dk mPNsn" (exposure of caste system) and dialogue with "xka/h th" provide historical precedent, showing Ambedkar's fight isn't isolated but continues a validated tradition of resistance. A wrong answer saying "Phule was Ambedkar's guru" or "they worked together" reveals confusion between personal mentorship and intellectual inheritance — the text never claims they met; Phule died in 1890, Ambedkar was born in 1891.

questions.q: Compare the roles of the school teacher (who asked the question) and the Maharaja of Baroda (who funded the scholarship) in shaping Ambedkar's trajectory. Which one represents "internal motivation" and which "external enablement"? Justify with textual evidence.
questions.a: The teacher triggers internal motivation — Ambedkar's three-part vow ("clerk, schools, awaken oppressed") originates entirely from within, sparked by the question. The Maharaja provides external enablement — the scholarship ("tedj i<+kbZ dhA") makes the vow actionable. The text juxtaposes them: "O;kid vè;;u ,oa ¯pru&euu osQ cy ij" (on teacher's advice AND Maharaja's support). A wrong answer swapping them or calling both "motivation" fails to distinguish agency (internal) from opportunity (external) — a distinction central to Ambedkar's own philosophy of self-help plus structural support.

questions.q: Write a 50-word paragraph introducing a "new supporting character" — a fictional Dalit student in 1920s Bombay who reads Ambedkar's essay and decides to pursue law. Use the same three-part structure Ambedkar used (profession, institution-building, awakening others) but adapt it to this character's context.
questions.a: "Ramji, a Mahar boy in 1920s Bombay, read Ambedkar's words and vowed: 'I will study law to fight cases for my people, start a night school in our basti so elders learn their rights, and organise youth to demand entry into the municipal water tank.'" A poor answer copies Ambedkar's exact words without adaptation — showing inability to transfer the structural pattern to a new context, which is the essence of "create" level thinking.
